items.hard_question: When two documents tie at the top after their positions from a lexical and a semantic search are combined, why is that not evidence that either one is better supported, and what should be done when the sources needed to settle the question are missing?

If every replica applies the same conflict-resolution rule and they all converge on an identical state, why can the outcome still be wrong for users, and in the limited-approval case what has already happened that choosing a later winner cannot undo?

When load can swing from about 100 to 400 requests per second and unit prices are unknown, what should make a capacity option count as too fragile to accept, and why is requests per second per machine a misleading way to report the result?

Why does adding the record of an event to publish only after the business transaction has already committed still leave a gap between the two, and what must consumers be ready to handle when the forwarding process retries?

A connection drops after a numbered update is sent but before the client acknowledges it. Why does resuming the session not by itself guarantee that no update was missed, and what should decide whether the gap is acceptable?
